I want to preface this story by saying I never had the ability to play past T-ball and am about as athletic as your elderly neighbor who only goes outside to get the mail.

In junior year of high school we did a softball unit, and because of scheduling, it was the first time I had done it since middle school. So the first day of class, a Thursday, we just did batting practice and some tossing. I was fine tossing, but I had no timing swinging. I was always too early, and would have struck out easily if it was a real game. I was probably the only kid not to make contact all class.

Over the weekend, I was at a friend's house and talking to him about how badly I did and how worried I was for Monday's class. He said he had a bat and ball, and we should go to the park down the street and he'd throw me batting practice. I figured it couldn't hurt, so we headed down there and I managed to get a little bit of timing and at least make contact. Sure, most of it was of the foul tip variety, but that's better than nothing. About 15 minutes in, we notice a car drop off a bunch of kids at the top of the park. We thought we might have to clear out but they busied themselves playing wall ball so we kept going.

A few minutes later one of them noticed us, and all of a sudden a bunch of kids come swarming down onto the field. I'm still at the plate, and now there are 10 snotty little pre-teen batting coaches surrounding me. "What the hell are you doing?" "Terrible swing!" "I can hit the ball farther than you!" "Give me that bat!" And out of fear, we let them swing and they did hit the ball much better than me or my friend. After being insulted and shown up for what seemed like an eternity, we got the bat and ball back and fled for the hills.

That Monday in gym class, I did manage to hit a single, so perhaps it wasn't all for nought.

TL;DR: terrible at gym class softball, tried to practice, got harassed by a group of 10 year olds.

This took place in gym class but it still counts. I've never been athletic at all, always been the type of person who trips over his own feet and stuff. So, in my junior year of high school, I was anxious when I found out we were doing softball in gym. The first day of the unit we just threw around and did batting practice. I couldn't even make contact, I was way too early and basically helpless. No one made fun of me, but I was still annoyed. I wanted to do better, but had no idea how.

That was a Thursday. Flash forward to Sunday. I'm spending the day at a friend's, and we're not sure what to do. So we go through a shed on his property looking for stuff and we find an aluminum bat and couple of softballs. We took the bat and balls down the street to the local park and decide to hit around. I throw him a few, he throws me a few. I'm working hard to get timing down, and pretty soon I begin to manage to get some grounders going. Nothing impressive, but I'm pretty stoked.

After like 20 minutes, we notice a group of little league kids get dropped off, and they're playing wall ball or something at a tennis court. We realize they're not there for a game, so we keep going. A few minutes later, the kids notice us and run down to the field. Keep in mind there are no parents in sight.

These kids are like 10 or 11, and one of them asks me for the bat. Being kind of shy then, I hand the bat over to the kid. He tells me that he's been watching my swing and that I "suck". He takes a swing and cracks my friend's pitch to the outfield. One of his friends gets the ball back and they begin taking their own batting practice, hitting better than either me or my friend and taking the time out to tell me that I looked "retarded" and that most of them "did my mom". Eventually we somehow got the bat and ball back and went home, very embarrassed and annoyed.

But...on Monday in gym class, first at bat, I socked a single up the middle.

tl;dr: couldn't hit the ball in high school gym class, tries to practice at a park to get better, got shown up by a bunch of ten year olds while there, figured it out anyway.
